decisions.evidence: Read the definition against its suppliers. The pairing convention is the published first-variable-linear one; U_T is an isometry so |lambda|=1 is derived, not assumed; integral invariance gives (lambda-1)int f=0 and the definition's two-case centering is correct (lambda=1 with nonconstant f, or lambda!=1 with int f=0). H0 is closed by Cauchy-Schwarz with the norm-one constant. Checked zero class excluded, eigenvalue-one constant, completed-Lebesgue orientation-only clause. Accepted.

Read all clauses: bounded, compact (subsequential norm convergence on bounded sequences), adjoint uniqueness by positive definiteness, self-adjoint, positive, isometry and unitary, invariant subspaces and orthogonal complements. The isometry-preserves-pairing derivation via ||f+g||^2 and ||f+ig||^2 is correct for the complex pairing. Checked H={0}, E={0}, the zero operator and that existence of an adjoint is not assumed. No simultaneous selection. Accepted.

Checked the minimizing-sequence step: the parallelogram identity applied to u=f-g_n, v=f-g_m uses (g_n+g_m)/2 in M and gives ||g_n-g_m||^2<2/n+2/m; completeness puts the limit in the closed M; the inner product (f-g)⊥M follows from minimality for real t and the substitution h->ih with <z,ih>=-i<z,h> for the first-variable-linear pairing. Uniqueness, linearity, contraction, M={0}, M=H and the zero space were checked. AC is used exactly for the minimizing sequence and completeness. Accepted.

Verified R=U(H) is closed (isometry maps Cauchy sequences to Cauchy sequences), U is injective, V=U^{-1}P_R is a contraction with VU=I and <Uf,g>=<f,Vg> obtained from the orthogonality of g-P_Rg to R (no representation theorem, no assumed surjectivity). Also checked M^perp=F in both directions via <h,h-Uh>=0 and the isometry identity, the decomposition H=M+F with P_F, A_N(I-U)g=(g-U^Ng)/N with the single-approximant epsilon argument, and the H={0} case. Accepted.

Checked the representative reduction (real and imaginary parts, infinite-value sets null and base-measurable), finite-simple approximation, the generating-algebra symmetric-difference step with at most 2q atoms incident to endpoints and error 2qb_r plus the reservoir, and the zero-pairing conclusion ||k||_2^2=| <k,k-R> |<=||k||_2 epsilon. No universal/a.e. quantifier exchange is used, and zero-total-measure factors give all-zero classes. Accepted.

Checked: product-measurable representative; a.e. square-integrable sections; Cauchy-Schwarz and Fubini giving ||K||<=||k||_2; class well-definedness under product-null changes and linearity; rectangle kernels are finite rank hence compact via finite Gram-Schmidt and successive real Bolzano-Weierstrass on finitely many coordinates; the nested-subsequence diagonal argument with the 2B2^{-m} splitting; operator-norm approximation; and injectivity of k->K by testing rectangles. Probability normalization is used where the text says so. Accepted.

Checked factor swap preserves the product sigma-algebra and the completion (null covers swap to null covers), ||k*||_2=||k||_2, the absolute-integrability check ||k(x,y)f(y)g(x)||_1<=||k||_2||f||_2||g||_2, Fubini with conjugation giving <Kf,g>=<f,Lg> where L has kernel k*, adjoint uniqueness, (K*)*=K, and both norm inequalities via sup_{||g||<=1}|<z,g>|=||z||. Checked z=0 and the zero kernel. Accepted.

Checked T x T preserves the completed product on generating rectangles and on null covers; the rectangle-tensor computation giving K_{Wl}=U K_l V and its extension by density and operator-norm convergence; K=UKV from Wk=k, hence KU=UK, and K*U=UK* from Wk*=k*; and the marginal argument giving K1=K*1=0, invariance of H0, and K_nonzero|H0 != 0 by splitting off the mean. The noninvertible case is handled by V=U^{-1}P_R, not surjectivity. Accepted.

Checked that the zero-image argument alone gives invariance of H0 for K and K*; that S=K*K is bounded with <Sf,g>=<Kf,Kg>=<f,Sg> and <Sf,f>=||Kf||^2>=0; that S is nonzero since some Kf0!=0 forces <Sf0,f0> >0; that compactness transfers from K through the continuous K*; and that SU=US follows from the two commutation relations. No eigenvalue of K itself is asserted. Accepted.

Re-derived the quadratic inequality |B(x,y)|^2<=q(x)q(y) including the q(y)=0 case; alpha=||S||=sup_{||x||=1}q(x)>0; ||Sx_n-alpha x_n||^2<=alpha(alpha-q(x_n)) with the maximizing sequence; the compactness extraction and limit giving Sx=alpha x with ||x||=1; and the contradiction from an infinite orthonormal family in the alpha-eigenspace (images at constant distance alpha*sqrt2). Checked S=0 is excluded, E is closed, and only one infinite selection (under AC) is used. Accepted.

Checked the chain: nonzero restriction of K to the nonzero closed H0; S=K*K nonzero positive compact self-adjoint commuting with U_T; the positive finite-dimensional eigenspace E; invariance of E from commutation; injectivity of U_T|E; rank-nullity giving equal image dimension and hence surjectivity onto E; and unitary of a surjective isometry. Checked E=ker(S-alpha I) for alpha>0 and that no invertibility of T is needed. Accepted.

Checked the finite-dimensional endomorphism supplier (algebraic closure supplied by the fundamental theorem), the single eigenvalue/eigenvector selection, ||Uf||=|lambda|||f|| forcing |lambda|=1 by positive definiteness, and the exclusion of f=c1 in H0 since c=int f=0 would make f=0. Checked dim E=1, E={0} excluded, and the no-AC note for a supplied E. Accepted.

Read all three implications and the density-zero reformulation. (i)=>(ii): a centered eigenfunction has |C_n(f0,f0)|=||f0||^2>0, so the absolute Cesaro mean cannot vanish (F8/F9). (ii)=>(iii): ergodicity from invariant indicators; a nonzero fixed product kernel is centered, injectivity gives K!=0; ergodicity makes K1,K*1 constant and Fubini makes their means zero, so the earlier chain produces a nonconstant eigenfunction. (iii)=>(ii): F=f0(x)conj(f0(y)) is fixed by W, has zero mean and nonzero norm. (iii)=>(i): projection of f0-otimes-conj(f0) onto constants vanishes, so the Cesaro mean of |<U^nf0,g>|^2 vanishes and finite Cauchy-Schwarz gives the absolute estimate. Step 5.1's density-zero equivalence (least cutoff integers, geometric partition) was checked. Accepted.

Reconstructed stages 0-2 explicitly: heights 1,4,13; widths 2/3,2/9,2/27; J_r taken from the left of the reservoir with the same width as the new levels; and the partition of [0,1) by the three thirds and the remaining reservoir. Checked h_r=(3^{r+1}-1)/2, tower mass 1-3^{-(r+1)}, reservoir 3^{-(r+1)}, that consecutive-level translations extend the stage-r partial map on each third, and that the new arrows from block tops to the next block's base/space are exactly the three new connections. Left-closed right-open levels give unique membership. Accepted.

Checked D_r,E_r increasing with complements of measure 3^{-r}, the union bijection T:D->E measurable and measure preserving on dyadic pieces (translations on disjoint pieces), the null wandering-set recursion B_{n+1}=B_n u T(B_n cap D) u T^{-1}(B_n cap E), and that X_0=[0,1)\B is invariant in both directions: if Tx in some B_n then x in B_{n+1}, and similarly for T^{-1}. Checked the identity extension is measurable and measure preserving by splitting preimages. No pointwise inverse selection is used. Accepted.

Checked the Borel-representative step, the finite-interval-union approximation, and the endpoint counting: the stage-r partition has atoms of length at most b_r, at most 2q atoms are incident to endpoints of the approximant, and removing the reservoir costs 3^{-(r+1)}, giving error < epsilon for large r. Checked the L2 density of level-constant functions on and off the tower and the high-density-level statement: with eta<delta mu(E)/(1+delta) the supposition of all levels at proportion <=1-delta gives mu(Q\E)>eta, contradicting the approximation. The delta>=1 case is immediate (any level with positive measure works, and the contradiction also closes for eta<mu(E)/2). Accepted.

Checked that a positive-measure strictly invariant E has a level of E-proportion >1-delta at every sufficiently late stage, that on the invariant conull set T^{k-j} transports E-measures between levels (so all levels share that density), and hence mu(E cap C_r)>(1-delta)mu(C_r) with mu(C_r)->1. Letting r grow gives mu(E)>=1-delta for every delta in (0,1), so mu(E)=1. Only one finite stage is needed per delta, and the null complements are removed first. Accepted.

Checked |f| invariant hence constant by ergodicity, normalization |f|=1, and the a.e. iterate identity f(T^kx)=lambda^k f(x) off a finite union of preimages of the original null set. The finite disk cover of the unit circle yields a positive-measure level E; the high-density level J with mu(J\E)<delta w_r and the two return times h_r on J^{(0)} and h_r+1 on J^{(1)} give |lambda^{h_r}-1|<2epsilon and |lambda^{h_r+1}-1|<2epsilon on positive-measure subsets, hence |lambda-1|<4epsilon for every epsilon>0. Then ergodicity forces f constant. Accepted.

Verified for every stage-r level union Q that the left thirds Q^{(0)} satisfy Q^{(0)} subset Q cap T^{-h_r}Q modulo the fixed null set (T^{h_r} maps left thirds to the corresponding middle thirds, both inside Q), giving mu(Q cap T^{-h_r}Q)>=mu(Q)/3. For A=L_{1,0}=[0,2/9), a union of stage-r levels for every r>=1, this gives at least 2/27>4/81=mu(A)^2 along h_r->infinity, so strong mixing fails for the fixed pair. The general liminf with 2eta_r and (7/3)eta_r was also checked. Accepted.

Checked the composition: the partial maps give an invertible completed Lebesgue probability system; every complex L2 eigenfunction of it is constant; the spectral equivalence then gives weak mixing with the absolute value inside the Cesaro mean; and the fixed interval [0,2/9) has correlations at least 2/27 against mu(A)^2=4/81 along unbounded heights, so the system is not strongly mixing. The identity/null modification from the construction leaves the measures unchanged. Accepted.

Checked the refutation: one fixed system (normalized Chacon) satisfies the hypothesis; the fixed pair A=B=[0,2/9) has d_{h_r}(A,A)>=2/81>0 along h_r->infinity, so the correlations do not converge to zero and the claimed conclusion fails. The refutation does not infer pointwise convergence from an average and uses the same AC scope as the witness. Accepted.
